name: dev.tekyous/tekyous
title: Tekyous
description: Generate tech stack diagrams, get stack recommendations, compare developer tools. Free, no sign-in.

tools.name: search_tools
tools.description: Search Tekyous's catalogue of developer tools by text, category, subcategory, pricing model and minimum scores (1–5). Text matches tool names and aliases first; when nothing matches, each word is looked for in names, summaries and categories ('static site hosting'). Includes products that belong to another tool (e.g. Streamlit Cloud, part of Streamlit). Returns matching tools with a one-line summary, category, pricing, scores and a tekyous.dev URL, plus the total number of matches. Use get_tool for one tool's full profile and compare_tools for two or three side by side; for whole stacks, use search_stacks.

query.description: A tool name, or a few words describing what it does
query.title: Query

min_popularity.description: Lowest popularity score: 1 = niche, 5 = known across the industry
min_popularity.title: Min Popularity

min_flexibility.description: Lowest flexibility score: 1 = opinionated, 5 = adapts to anything
min_flexibility.title: Min Flexibility

min_performance.description: Lowest performance score: 1 = slow or heavy, 5 = best in class
min_performance.title: Min Performance

min_portability.description: Lowest portability score: 1 = locked to one vendor, 5 = runs or moves anywhere
min_portability.title: Min Portability

tools.name: get_tool
tools.description: Get one tool's full profile from Tekyous by slug: description, key features, pros and cons, pricing tiers, scores (1–5) with their reasoning, related tools (alternatives, integrations, tools it works with) and curated stacks that use it. Returns the tool page URL and a builder link that opens the tool on the canvas. search_tools finds the slug; to weigh two or three tools against each other, use compare_tools.

slug.description: Tool slug, e.g. 'postgresql'; search_tools finds it
slug.title: Slug

tools.name: compare_tools
tools.description: Compare two or three tools from Tekyous's catalogue side by side, by slug: for each, the summary, categories, pricing model and tiers, scores (1–5) with their reasoning, key features, pros and cons, license and its tekyous.dev URL; plus how the tools relate to each other in the catalogue (alternatives, integrations, works with) and the score differences. search_tools finds the slugs; for one tool, get_tool gives the full profile.

slugs.description: Two or three tool slugs, e.g. ['supabase', 'firebase']
slugs.title: Slugs

tools.name: get_stack
tools.description: Get a curated tech stack from Tekyous by slug: its core tools per category, the alternatives offered for parts of it (options) and optional additions, scores with reasoning, pricing and FAQs. Returns the stack page URL and a builder link that opens the stack on the canvas. search_stacks finds the slug; to get a stack picked for a project type and experience level, use recommend_stack.

tools.name: search_stacks
tools.description: Search Tekyous's curated tech stacks by text (a stack name, or a tool the stack uses), stack type, experience level and project type. A tool name finds the stacks built around it first, then those offering it as an option, then as an add-on, as the tekyous.dev catalogue ranks them. Returns each stack's name, slug, tagline, type, level, project type, popularity and learning-curve scores, its main tools, and its page and builder links, plus the total number of matches. get_stack reads one in full. To get a stack picked for a project rather than browse, use recommend_stack.

query.description: A stack name, or a tool the stack should use, e.g. 'django' or 'ollama'
query.title: Query

stack_type.description: Stack type slug: 'project' (an app's whole stack), 'infrastructure' (self-hosted or platform setups), 'developer' (a coding agent or developer setup)
stack_type.title: Stack Type

experience_level.description: Experience level key: non_technical, beginner, intermediate, advanced
experience_level.title: Experience Level

project_type.description: Project type key, e.g. web_app, website, api_only, ai_agent
project_type.title: Project Type

tools.name: recommend_stack
tools.description: Recommend a tech stack for a project type and an experience level, using the same data as the tekyous.dev questionnaire. Returns the editors' notes on that combination (`context`) and its approaches: distinct ways to build it (e.g. Full-Stack Framework, Backend-First, Backend as a Service), each a complete stack on its own. Approaches are alternatives to each other: pick one, or lay them out as options, never combine their tools into one stack. Per approach, each category lists the recommended tools in rank order, with rationale and caveats, then ranked alternatives that could replace them; an approach comes with a builder link that opens it as an editable diagram and the diagram spec behind it. A combination without named approaches returns one, with no key or name. Unknown values come back with the list of valid ones.

project_type.description: Project type key: web_app, website, mobile_app, api_only, ai_agent, automation, data_pipeline, dashboard, ml_project, browser_extension
project_type.title: Project Type

experience_level.description: Experience level key: non_technical, beginner, intermediate, advanced
experience_level.title: Experience Level

preferred_language.description: Language tool slug the stack should use, e.g. 'python'
preferred_language.title: Preferred Language

tools.name: compose_diagram
tools.description: Draw a tech stack diagram: a picture and an editable diagram on tekyous.dev. By default it shows the stack: catalogue tool slugs (look each up with search_tools) in three to five groups named by role, with no connectors, no numbered steps and at most two notes; connectors only when the user asks how the parts connect. A custom tool is a technology the catalogue lacks, under its own short name with what it does in its caption, never a step, module or feature of the project. Pass the spec as `diagram` (format 'tekyous-diagram'; the design_stack prompt explains it) or a full Tekyous canvas file. Returns an image URL (PNG), a builder link that opens the diagram fully editable, slugs the catalogue does not know, `custom_matches` (custom tools the catalogue lists, each with the `change` that swaps it in: apply it), warnings from the catalogue's rules, layout `issues` in the drawn picture, `advice` (where the spec strays from a plain stack: follow it unless the user asked for that), the look used with the others available (`look`: mention them to the user), and the document to send again when revising. In hosts that render MCP Apps, the result shows as the Tekyous diagram widget: the picture in the chat, inline and full screen, with an Open in builder button, so the reply needs no image of its own (no image URL, markdown or HTML image). Elsewhere, give the image URL and the builder link.

diagram.description: The short form: tools by slug in groups, with custom tools for what the catalogue lacks. No positions; Tekyous lays it out (a full canvas file, format tekyous-canvas, places everything itself). By default a stack: groups by role, no connectors, one or two notes at most.

color.description: A palette key or a #rrggbb colour. Nothing else (no CSS).

toolSlug.description: A tool slug from the Tekyous catalogue, e.g. "postgresql". An unknown slug becomes a placeholder card and is reported back.

categorySlug.description: A catalogue category or subcategory slug, e.g. "databases".

id.description: Your own id, unique in the diagram. Tool slugs are ids too.

caption.description: A short line under the card.

title.description: Shown as a large bold title above the diagram.

titleAlign.description: center or right spans the title across the diagram.

titleColor.description: The title colour; near-white when left out.

template.description: layered: one frame per group, in the order given and the direction below; without groups, the catalogue layers (frontend, backend, data, hosting, AI). by-category: one frame per catalogue category; do not send groups with it.

direction.description: How the groups follow each other. left-to-right: each group a column, side by side. top-to-bottom: each group a band, stacked.

align.description: left-to-right only: where the columns start. top: one top edge, each column as tall as its tools. center: centred on the tallest, so connectors between groups run level. Leave out: top, or center when a connector joins two groups.

preset.description: What a card shows: detailed (name, category, subcategory, pricing), standard (name, category, pricing), simple (logo and name), tile (logo over name), icon (logo only).

outline.description: none: logos and names without a card border.

background.description: The canvas ground: dark (navy, the default) or light (sand), for example for a picture that goes on a light page such as a README or a doc.

cardBg.description: One background colour for every card that sets none of its own (a tool's own bg wins). Left out: the standard navy card. Not shown with outline none.

groups.description: Frames, each holding its tools: a column (left-to-right) or a band (top-to-bottom), in the order given; a side group sits next to the group it names instead.

connectors.description: Leave out unless the user asks how the parts connect (data flow, requests, architecture). Then join neighbouring groups, with labels of one or two words.

notes.description: Leave out by default; one or two at most, for decisions worth explaining.

spec.description: The short form: tools by slug in groups, with custom tools for what the catalogue lacks. No positions; Tekyous lays it out (a full canvas file, format tekyous-canvas, places everything itself). By default a stack: groups by role, no connectors, one or two notes at most.

bg.description: Card background, to set a tool apart: a colour, or transparent for no background.

logoScale.description: Logo size: 1 is normal, 1.5 half again as big.

name.description: The technology's own short name (e.g. "HTTPX"); past about 20 characters it is cut off on the card. What it does here goes in caption.

icon.description: One of database, server, cloud, globe, lock, mail, code, box, queue, chart, user, bolt; or one letter or digit; or up to four emoji.

bg.description: Card background, to set a tool apart: a colour, or transparent for no background.

logoScale.description: Logo size: 1 is normal, 1.5 half again as big.

specCustomTool.description: A technology the catalogue does not list (look it up with search_tools first), such as your own service. Never one of the project's steps, modules or features: those are not tools.

title.description: One or two words naming a role (App, Data, AI, Hosting), not a numbered step.

color.description: Frame colour: a palette key or any #rrggbb. Left out, each group gets a different one, in an order of the diagram's own, from sky, emerald, violet, amber, rose, #fb923c, #2dd4bf, #f472b6, #818cf8, #a3e635, #22d3ee, #e879f9.

fill.description: How much the frame colour fills it: none (an outline), soft, strong or solid.

titlePlace.description: above: the title sits over the frame's top edge.

titleColor.description: The group title colour; grey when left out.

side.description: The id of a main group this one supports (a contact form service, analytics, email). It takes no column or band of its own: it sits under that group (left-to-right) or to its right (top-to-bottom), only as big as its tools.

from.description: A tool slug, custom tool id, group id or note id.

near.description: The tool slug, custom tool id or group id the note sits beside.

tools.name: revise_diagram
tools.description: Change a diagram made with compose_diagram without writing it out again: pass its `document` (as returned) and a list of changes: add, remove, replace or move a tool, connect or disconnect two, add a note, add or remove a group, or set the title, the look or a group's title and colour ({"disconnect": "all"} makes it a plain stack again). Changes apply in order. Returns the same as compose_diagram (image URL, builder link, checks, advice, look, the revised document) and, in hosts that render MCP Apps, shows the revised picture in the same widget. A change that doesn't fit says which one and what the diagram has instead.

diagram.description: The diagram to change: the `document` compose_diagram returned

changes.description: Edits applied in order. Tools are named by slug (catalogue tools) or id (custom tools); groups by id. Examples: {"add": "redis", "to": "data"}; {"add": {"id": "worker", "name": "Worker", "icon": "server"}, "to": "app"}; {"remove": "mongodb"}; {"replace": "vercel", "with": "netlify"}; {"move": "stripe", "to": "services"}; {"set": {"title": "Acme tech stack", "display": {"preset": "standard"}}}; {"set": {"display": {"background": "light"}}}; {"group": "data", "set": {"title": "Storage", "color": "emerald"}}; {"add_group": {"id": "ai", "title": "AI", "tools": ["openai"]}, "after": "app"}; {"remove_group": "ops"}; {"connect": {"from": "nextjs", "to": "postgresql", "label": "reads"}}; {"disconnect": {"from": "nextjs", "to": "postgresql"}}; {"disconnect": "all"}; {"note": {"near": "data", "text": "Managed Postgres after launch"}}.

add.description: A catalogue slug, a tool entry ({slug, caption, ...}) or a custom tool ({id, name, icon, ...})

remove.description: Slug or custom tool id; its connectors and notes go too

replace.description: Slug or custom tool id, replaced in the same place

with.description: For replace: a catalogue slug, a tool entry or a custom tool

to.description: For add and move: the group id (leave out on add for the diagram's own tools)

set.description: Fields to change: on the diagram (title, titleAlign, titleColor, template, direction, align, display), or with group on that group (title, color, fill, border, titleAlign, titlePlace, titleSize, titleColor, side). null removes a field; display is merged

group.description: For set: the group id to change

add_group.description: A new group, as in the spec ({id, title, tools, custom, ...})

after.description: For add_group: the group id it follows (else it goes last)

remove_group.description: Group id; its tools, their connectors and notes go too

connect.description: A connector, as in the spec ({from, to, label, line, ...}); replaces one between the same two

disconnect.description: {from, to}: the connector to remove; "all" removes every connector

note.description: A note, as in the spec ({text, near})
